creative.anti_copy_boundary: Factory imagery and spaghetti-path drawing → reported project percentages → headline and closing slogan → red/green shop-floor composition
creative.argument_sequence: Challenge the assumption that simple tools are weak → show the hidden waste → show the improved flow → offer reported project impacts → explain the observation method → make the human change mechanism explicit
creative.attention_mechanism: The oversized headline asks a provocative question, then the red, tangled factory paths visually prove chaos immediately. The reader can see the argument before reading the words.
creative.emotional_trigger: Lean practitioners recognise a familiar frustration: a sophisticated organisation can overlook an embarrassingly visible source of waste.
creative.lived_work_moment: invisible waste → abstract debate → friction without a shared picture → need for action
creative.reader_payoff: A practical way to turn a vague process-waste conversation into an observable team exercise.
creative.transferable_atoms: Make an invisible operational failure physically visible before explaining it. → Use a true before/after with a shared scene so the reader can see what changed. → Treat evidence and method as support for a visual discovery, not as the opening hook. → End with the human change mechanism: what seeing the process makes possible.
creative.utility: Use during a Lean/warehouse workshop → Share with an improvement lead → Return to follow the six-step observation method → Use the before/after logic to frame a local problem

media.availability_note: Manually reviewed Top-100 visual asset mapped to TOP100-065: references/top 100/65.jpeg.

review.evidence: Asset-specific attention, composition, craft, and recombination observations are recorded in this file; the calibration rationale is documented in CALIBRATION-REVIEW.md. See references/creative-review/top100-forensics/TOP100-065.json.

visual.composition: Two-column Lean poster with a large red tangled before-state factory scene, a green after-state scene, impact panels and a short observation method.
visual.craft_notes: The before/after is a causal visual narrative, not a decorative comparison. → The red/green coding holds across illustration, headers and performance signals. → The method is deliberately subordinate to the visual discovery moment.
visual.eye_path: provocative headline → red before-state map → green after-state map → right-side impact comparison → bottom six-step method → closing line
visual.hierarchy: The visual problem is largest; numbers and methods support it. This keeps the page from becoming a generic Lean cheat sheet.
visual.imagery: The plant scenes are explanatory models. People, materials and stations make the travel paths emotionally and operationally legible.
visual.layout: Magazine-style two-column board. The left two-thirds carries the large before/after factory scenes; the right third carries why/impact/gain panels; the final lower band gives a short method and a concluding value statement.
visual.pacing: The graphic has a strong entry scene, then moves into dense support. It rewards a fast reader with one clear message and a slower reader with method and proof.
visual.technical_treatment: Red/green performs more than branding: it encodes chaos versus flow. Industrial dark-blue labels frame white panels and make the page feel procedural and concrete.
visual.typography: Condensed heavy uppercase headline and clear sectional labels create a shop-floor poster feel. Brush-stroke emphasis is used sparingly to turn one sentence into a maxim.
visual.visual_mechanism: The physical route diagram is the evidence. It demonstrates how a pen-on-layout reveals unnecessary movement much more powerfully than a summary KPI.

creative.anti_copy_boundary: Forecasting/planning/buying wording and examples → source's specific column treatment → source typography and category labels → source caption rhetoric
creative.argument_sequence: Name a conflation → separate the three jobs → show the hand-off relationship → connect misalignment to inventory and cash consequences → invite the reader to identify their own weakest link
creative.attention_mechanism: Three large, adjacent labels—Forecasting, Planning and Buying—signal a distinction the reader likely feels but has not cleanly named.
creative.emotional_trigger: Operational people recognise the sentence-level conflict: 'the forecast changed' versus 'the order is already placed.'
creative.lived_work_moment: conceptual confusion → cross-functional disagreement → need for shared vocabulary
creative.reader_payoff: A reusable way to clarify accountability and escalation in a forecasting-to-buying process.
creative.transferable_atoms: Start with three terms readers casually conflate. → Force each term through the same decision schema. → Use the final shared section to expose the failure at the hand-off, not within an individual function. → Let the caption provide a lived scenario the comparison itself cannot show.
creative.utility: Useful in a meeting where terms are being conflated → Easy to send to a planner/buyer counterpart → Acts as a concise onboarding reference

review.evidence: Asset-specific attention, composition, craft, and recombination observations are recorded in this file; the calibration rationale is documented in CALIBRATION-REVIEW.md. See references/creative-review/top100-forensics/TOP100-013.json.

visual.composition: High-contrast three-column comparison table with repeated decision rows and a shared conclusion.
visual.craft_notes: The columns are genuinely comparable, not three unrelated text boxes. → The content is compressed into decision-relevant categories rather than encyclopaedic detail. → The reader can stop at any lane and still retain a complete local answer.
visual.eye_path: Question/title → Forecasting lane → Planning lane → Buying lane → shared lower conclusion
visual.hierarchy: Large functional labels create first-level scan; short descriptors and row labels create second-level scan; supporting details remain subordinate.
visual.imagery: Minimal. The visual primitive is a table/comparison, which is the proof mechanism.
visual.layout: A single-page comparison board: high-contrast title area above three equal vertical lanes. Each lane follows the same row order, with a dark category label at the top/side and a compact block of information below.
visual.pacing: Fast entry, then controlled vertical reading. Repetition reduces cognitive switching despite a high information load.
visual.technical_treatment: Restrained white surface with dark anchors and separated lanes; colour is used for categorical separation rather than mood.
visual.typography: Bold high-contrast sans-serif labels, intentionally stronger than explanatory copy. This is a reading interface, not a poster.
visual.visual_mechanism: The equal columns prove that the three activities are related but non-identical; the graphic makes the boundary visible before the caption explains the consequence.
